headline: AMD chief executive Lisa Su said in Taipei that the company will substantially increase its chip supply in 2027 and needs more advanced chip-making capacity to meet demand.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: the chief executive's own on-the-record remarks, reported by Reuters, though without figures or named deals.
importance_line: Businesses and cloud providers waiting for AI servers depend on how much chip supply AMD can secure, and Su says it needs more advanced manufacturing capacity, but she gave no figures and no agreement with TSMC was announced.
summary: Reuters reports that AMD chief executive Lisa Su told reporters in Taipei on 6 Oct 2026 that the company, Nvidia's closest rival in AI processors, will "substantially increase" its chip supply in 2027 and needs more advanced wafer capacity, the silicon discs chips are cut from, because demand will stay very high for several years. She had met the electronics maker Foxconn and was due to meet TSMC, the Taiwanese contract chipmaker that makes AMD's advanced processors, but gave no figures.
notes: Pool item DigiTimes (paywalled) is the same trip; credited to Reuters, whose wire text was read in KELO-AM's copy. Sources differ on her arrival date (DigiTimes 5 Oct; Taiwan News and BigGo 6 Oct) and on when she leaves for South Korea (Reuters 6 Oct; Taiwan News and BigGo 8 Oct). Su's statements are plans, not figures.
